{"triples":[{"subject":"Linear Regression Models","predicate":"uses","object":"lm function","object_type":"Other","source_sentence":"Ordinary linear regression models were fitted with the lm function in R."},{"subject":"Regression Model","predicate":"uses","object":"log-transformed by-item average RTs","object_type":"Other","source_sentence":"The baseline regression model was first fitted with log-transformed by- item average RTs as the dependent variable and control predictors as independent variables."},{"subject":"Regression Model","predicate":"uses","object":"cumulative surprisal","object_type":"Other","source_sentence":"For each computational model, the target regression model was then fitted with cumulative surprisal as the independent variable of interest on top of control predictors in the baseline regression model."},{"subject":"Sentence Processing","predicate":"uses","object":"self-paced reading or eye-tracking experiments","object_type":"Other","source_sentence":"In sentence processing , the processing costs of words within sentences can be easily measured with self-paced reading or eye-tracking experiments, but the processing costs of morphemes within words cannot, so that cumulative surprisal should be computed to transform processing costs from morphemes to words."},{"subject":"Log-likelihood ratio","predicate":"uses","object":"nested model comparisons","object_type":"Other","source_sentence":"Therefore, the cumulative surprisal estimated by computational models was evaluated with nested model comparisons via log-likelihood ratio tests based on the χ2-distribution with df = 1, the difference in the number of parameters between two nested regression models."}]}

{"triples":[{"subject":"Computational Models","predicate":"uses","object":"cumulative surprisal","object_type":"Concept","source_sentence":"In this paper, we performed a computational simulation experiment with human RTs in visual lexical decision experiments available from the ELP , a \"shared task\" in the morphological processing literature, and evaluated computational models with different representational assumptions via cumulative surprisal as a linking hypothesis , in order to investigate whether morphological processing tracks morphemes and parses them into hierarchical syntactic structures ."}]}
